R3-docs.summary:
R3-docs is done. Every edit is measured, and every changed check was shown to fail on a case that must fail and then pass. Nothing was written under build/native or bench/runs, no make was run in the repo's serializer/, and no git command was used.

1. BENCH. The rotate in bench/compat.lua and bench/oc/compat.lua is now the masked-piece form, `(a >> n) | ((a << (32 - n)) & 0xFFFFFFFF)`. The `a = a & 0xFFFFFFFF` line and the n == 0 case are kept, and a header note says why.
   - The OC sha256 benchmark, loaded the harness's way, gives 4044b974...5a5d with the new compat [M] on: round 3 (JIT on and off), R2's hint build, the round-2 32-bit build, PUC 5.3.6 (Windows and Linux) and PUC 5.4.8.
   - With the old compat, round 3 raises `[string "compat-bitops"]:11: result of '|' has more than 53 significant bits` [M]. So do run-standalone.sh's sha256 row and its contract.lua and compat-branches.lua gates, which pass with the new compat [M].
   - The harness evidence in bench/runs/2026-10-17-bitop (read only) shows p1-sha256 failing in all five round-3 arms on the operator path; the stock arm (bit32 path) passed.
   - Old and new rrotate return the same value in every call where the old one does not raise, over 320,128 calls on every VM above. The old one raised 80,234 times on round 3; the new one never does, even with operands in [-2^32, 2^32).
   - No other operator in either file, and no other bench, bench/oc or Scala-embedded Lua, has an intermediate that can pass 53 bits. The only operator use in the Scala is the d5 probe, whose raises are deliberate.

2. THE HINT.
   - serializer/tests/bitop.lua now requires the whole new message at the end of the error. It FAILS 6/1 on a scratch erislj_test linked against build/native (no hint) and PASSES 7/7 against R2's hint archive. The old check passed both builds, so it could not see the hint.
   - The d5 classifier in OcljSmoke.scala still works by substring: the expected line is unchanged and matched on build/native and on R2's hint build, JIT on and off. The round-2 build still fails it.
   - The Scala compiles: javac then scalac 2.13.11 on JDK 17 into a fresh directory gives exit 0, 26 class files and 5 deprecations, the same as the pre-edit copy. A one-token sabotage gives exit 1.

3. README dialect section.
   - The rotate is the main example of U1-B's cost, with the exact rule: right rotations by 1-10 and left by 22-31 raise; right by 11-31 and left by 1-21 never do; and a right rotation by 0 written as the idiom also raises.
   - It states that unmodified 5.3 code raises here, that PUC 5.3.6 computes it, and that the round-2 build computed it modulo 2^32 (BitOp's signed form).
   - It gives the one-mask remedy for both directions.
   - The xorshift64 example is fixed (it raises at its second step), and "masks to 32 bits" now says masking each shifted piece or operand.
   - The __name deviation is added.
   - Every new example was measured on round 3, the hint build and PUC 5.3.6.
   - I added one thing the brief did not ask for: FNV-1a 32-bit gives a wrong value with no error (4030533980 here, 3582672807 on PUC), because the double product is rounded before the mask.

4. ROADMAP.
   - Rows 146, 206, 208 and 210 are corrected as the review's verdicts say.
   - Row 208 gains the rotate finding, the hint and R1's jit.util tooling patch.
   - All 13 TODO-MEASURE placeholders are kept (3 README, 10 roadmap), and no numbers were invented.

NOTICE now lists lib_jit.c, which R1's patch-bitop-jitlib.sh changes. serializer/README.md now quotes the whole message the test checks. LuaJITStateFactory.java is unchanged because it never quotes the message. CR=0 in every file.

R2-tests.summary:
R2-tests is done. All three runners pass on a scratch build that has the hint, and the new negctl arm is caught by its catchers on R1's build.

What I changed:
- **The hint.** Every X rule now raises the new text exactly: `result of '<op>' has more than 53 significant bits (mask each operand to 32 bits first)`.
  - The X rules are in t_ops, t_fold, t_sar, drv, t_jit2 and bitfuzz.
  - The checks that only classify the error now match up to "bits": t_jit2's KIND, bitfuzz's errkind, and drv's kind (which already did).
  - The exact text is pinned in four places: the .expect files (the matrix compares them exactly); xrule.lua, which requires X's whole text on PUC; bitop_test.c BT3a-d; and a new run-bitop part-1 check that every inexact line of each .expect carries the hint.
- **The .expect files** were re-derived mechanically with C1's method: PUC 5.3.6 X run, reword.lua, deviation lines from the hint build. [M] Each regenerated file equals the old file with the hint appended to every inexact line, byte for byte: t_ops 550 lines, t_fold 11, t_sar 5.
  - Part 2's provenance lists exactly deviations.txt: 2, 10 and 0 ids.
- **The review's test fixes**, all applied:
  - run-bitfuzz.sh: any nonzero exit from our side is now 1; the JIT-on file's #cov line must say 'jit on' (else 2); 0 seeds, cases or tuples are refused.
  - bitfuzz-cmp.lua: it scans for #end before reading any tuple, so a cut file is CRASH (exit 1), and a missing field counts as a mismatch instead of raising.
  - run-bitjit.sh: ndiff counts both directions; 0 seeds or cases are refused; the header now says about 42 MB.
  - negctl-bitop.sh: 0 knobs are refused; it says about 40 MB a gen run; there is a new INEXACT-BNOT arm; R1's seventh patch is in the reproduction check and object map (lib_jit.c → lib_jit.o).
  - t_fold LEX: PUC now prints an integer with %d in X mode too, xrule's no-operator branch requires the X result to equal the raw one, and LEX accepts a 16-digit decimal id. The three wide literals (0x7fffffffffffffff, 9007199254740993, 9223372036854775807) are now in deviations.txt.
  - LUA_INIT and LUA_INIT_5_3 are unset at the top of all three runners.

Results [M]:
- **Hint build (hint build b-hint: build/native copy, lj_meta.o rebuilt, relinked):** run-bitop PASS, run-bitjit PASS (40 s, 41,580,593 bytes), run-bitfuzz PASS.
- **Old-message build (a byte-identical copy of build/native, luajit.exe md5 add0bf85d648):** run-bitop FAILs (matrix 550/11/5 lines, BT3a-d). run-bitjit and run-bitfuzz pass by design, because they only classify the error.
- **negctl-bitop.sh on a copy of R1's finished build (b-r1, luajit.exe md5 dfee3ca465e1, which matches the repo's sources):** with OCLJ_NEGCTL_ARMS=INEXACT-BNOT, setup passed (all seven patch scripts reproduce the build). Canon passed with every round-3 object reproduced, INEXACT-BNOT was caught by t_ops, t_fold and fuzz:V, and restore passed. Exit 0 in 74 s.

The full 27-arm negctl run is left to the main session.
